upstream_source.scope: Windows post-relaunch wait and old process incarnation only; N52 maps process classification and N54 maps test-only spawn admission.

contract: A mapped Windows Gateway relaunch is verified only after its original (pid, create_time) incarnation is no longer live and a fresh fleet snapshot is read. The bounded wait covers the detached watcher's 120-second deadline plus 30 seconds while that incarnation is pending. PID reuse, unreadable identity, a stale row, and strict discovery failure cannot authorize a replacement claim. Verified siblings retain restart eligibility. Before _pause_windows_gateways_for_update can return its recovery token, any late drain, force-stop, or SCM stop failure must recover already-paused ordinary gateways; only actually-attempted unmapped stops may be replayed, SCM-owned launcher trees remain outside the ordinary force-stop set, and rollback failures remain visible.
source_and_caller: hermes_cli/gateway.py:_spawn_gateway_restart_watcher waits for the old incarnation and declines a second launch if it remains live at the deadline.

hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:_pause_windows_gateways_for_update captures strict identities, excludes SCM-owned gateway launchers from ordinary stop ownership, journals ordinary recovery before pause side effects, and recovers that journal on late pause failure; _resume_windows_gateways_after_update passes old identities to mapped watchers, and _poll_fleet_versions_with_relaunch_budget retries if the old incarnation exits during collection.
gateway/status.py:_pid_identity_is_live distinguishes PID reuse and treats unreadable identity as pending; generic manual profile and command-line fallback callers propagate this identity.
